maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
There was nothing filed in the office, and there is nothing in the office now, to indicate any such intention in the mind of my hon. friend. Furthermore, his own officials in the department advised me to the contrary. I was told by the proper officers as to what my duty was in the premises, and I followed their advice.
Mr. IllN FRFT: I repeat that there was not the least authority in the department to

permit my hon. friend either to appoint a new commissioner or to make those payments. I may tell my hon. friend that the reason we did not ask the house for an amount sufficient to pay a new commissioner was that when we decided to hold a general election we did not think it would be proper for a commissioner to be going around different parts of the country hearing certain cases while the election was pending.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: But you intended to proceed as soon as the elections were over and you were returned to power.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
Yes, by asking the house to vote a sum sufficient for the salary of the new commissioner. In the first place I claim that there was no authority for this government to appoint a new commissioner, and certainly there was no authority for the government to make payments before this house had an opportunity to discuss the matter. I do not like to protest, because I am not against the payment of the claims, but I wish payment had been made in the regular way.
The other point I wish to make is this: I was blamed, as Secretary of State, and the previous government were blamed, for delay. The delays came about mainly because we wished to proceed in the regular way.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: Nonsense.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: We had to file the report, as the hon. member for Queens-Lunenburg knows; we had to give hon. members time to read and digest the report and we had to put through the bill. There was a good deal of discussion in connection with the bill; it had to be adopted by the Senate, and all these things had to be done before any payments were made. In this case, however, my hon. friend chose the easiest way by appointing his own commissioner, sending him away to hear the cases and paying the awards before the house even approved of the appointment of the commissioner.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: So far as my memory goes, this house never approved of the findings of Mr. Friel or Mr. Pugsley; those were approved by order in council and money was voted by parliament to cover the awards.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: There we are in full agreement.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
We followed the same procedure. What would have been the result if we had delayed? If we had not proceeded, as I was advised by the permanent officials of the department we should proceed, and as I was advised by the auditor general and

Supply-Secretary of State
the law officers I was entitled to proceed, to-day my hon. friend would be blaming me for having held up payment of these awards. I went in there to clean up the work of this department as far as I could, and I have cleaned it from top to bottom in connection with this business. I hope, with health and strength, during the ensuing summer, to end these reparation claims and have them finally settled, so that we will have no further trouble or difficulty with them. That has been my aim; I was told that was my duty, and I have spent day after day until late at night, from early morning, performing that duty.
I do not wish to discuss the former commissioner, but when I went to the department I found a commissioner who could not go on with the work; who had certain disputes outstanding as to his commission; who alleged that he had been orally authorized in certain ways and who, I think, was quite unwilling to go on under the circumstances and carry out his work. I made a compromise with him in regard to his personal claims, which he was then proceeding in the exchequer court to recover. I saw by the correspondence that there was an entire difference of opinion between the commissioner and my predecessor; I saw that there was some dispute as to my predecessor's views with regard to the compensation payable to the commissioner; I saw that the Minister of Justice had given an opinion contrary to that of my hon. friend, and I thought the best course was to compromise the commissioner's claim, close it up and end it without further discussion.
I hope my hon. friend is not going to force me into a discussion of the final arrangements with Commissioner Friel and the conditions under which they were made. There were a large number of claims filed. The department was prepared to go on and deal with them. Mr. Friel having declined to go on except under conditions with which my hon. friend had refused to comply, a new commissioner was appointed, a full settlement was made with Commissioner Friel and a release in full taken for all his claims. The new commissioner proceeded with his work; he has carried it on assiduously from day to day and week to week. Those claims were outstanding; they were recognized by the then government, as they are recognized by the present government; and it seems to me it is the duty of the Secretary of State to secure a final winding up of all these claims at the earliest possible date. That I have been endeavouring to do.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
I do not want to prolong this discussion unduly, but there are two 22110-188
points in connection with which I disagree entirely with my hon. friend, and other points in connection with which I disagree to a certain extent.
The two points in connection with which I disagree with him are these: In the first place I do not admit that my hon. friend has followed, as he has said, the same procedure in connection with this new commissioner as we followed in connection with the old. I have explained very fully that we tabled the report of the former commissioner; it was read by the house and studied by any hon. member who desired to do so. Later on I brought down a bill, and following that an estimate, covering the claims which had been heard and the decisions which had been tabled in the house.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
After protests had been
made time and again because of the delay.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
Perhaps so; perhaps we
were a bit slow in doing all that, but my contention is that my hon. friend has proceeded too quickly. He has appointed a commissioner when there was no salary voted for him; he has received a report from that commissioner and has paid the awards recommended without the house being given the opportunity of discussing them. Perhaps they were right. I have no fault to find with any of them. But that is not the only point in regard to which I disagree with my hon. friend. We have here an instance of the same form of government against which we have protested in other cases. The minister has followed the example of his leader and has dealt with the matter without the least regard for parliament. He did not see fit to wait until parliament should authorize him, either by a majority or unanimously, to go on with the work. He has dealt with the matter in his own way. In his own inimitable style he has undertaken to clean the department-and I do not admit for a moment that it needed cleaning to that extent. But once he got there he thought he had become czar or mikado of the Secretary of State's department and he went ahead with the work of cleaning up. And he cleaned it up so fast that he forgot that before doing anything of the kind it was his duty to come to parliament and receive authorization. I do not wish to take issue with my hon. friend unnecessarily; I have a great respect for him. But in the heat of discussion he sometimes uses words that are beyond the bounds of discretion. This afternoon he thought that the ex-Minister of Justice was nonsensical-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)

speechtext: Supply-Secretary of State

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: I did not say so. My hon. friend cannot get by with that. What I said was that it was nonsensical to assume that the people of St. John and Halifax would put a certain interpretation upon what the leader of the government had said. I never said that the ex-Minister of Justice or anyone else was nonsensical. I withdrew it as a personal remark with regard to the hon. member for Quebec South, who elicited it. But I said it was nonsensical to assume that, under the conditions in which the statement was made, the people would put upon the words of the Prime Minister the interpretation which was then suggested.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: Well, let that pass. Now the hon. gentleman tells me his duty was to clean up the department over which I had presided. He could not wait for parliament to authorize him. He could not follow the ordinary course and submit a bill or an estimate, taking parliament into his confidence. He had to do the work before parliament met. That is why I have raised the question. It is another instance where this government has simply taken into its hands an authority which does not belong to it. It has not waited for parliament to authorize the course it has taken. Without going into the past, I was merely asking the hon. gentleman to table a report by Commissioner McDougall before asking the house to vote a further amount to pay the awards that were allowed. I merely wanted him to take parliament into his confidence. I do not think it would be right for my hon. friend to ask for half a million to meet decisions which Commissioner McDougall may arrive at this fall. With every sympathy for the claimants, I say that the claims should wait until parliament knows something about '*hem and passes upon them.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: My hon. friend has raised an issue. This parliament never approved of the awards made by Mr. Pugsley-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: Certainly it did.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: Or Mr. Friel.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: Certainly.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
I beg the hon. member's
pardon.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
Parliament passed a bill
based on that very report. If my hon. friend will look at the statute he will find that the bill mentions the report.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
It mentions the report.
But that appropriation of $500,000 had no conditions attached to it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: That was a revote of a balance.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
It was not appropriated
for any specific purpose except to pay illegal warfare claims on proper findings. That was the opinion of the permanent officers of the department, who so advised me. The matter was taken up with the auditor general and the claims were paid. Personally I am glad they were paid; otherwise life would have been quite unhappy for me in view of the protests made against delay by members on both sides of the house. Now, what we propose to do is this-and there is no misunderstanding about it. I have asked the treasury board, the Minister of Finance, to enter an amount in the supplementary estimates to pay, during the present fiscal year, these reparation claims arising out of illegal warfare. I do not know whether the report dealing with, I believe, some 70 civil claims, will be ready before this session terminates. But I have urged the commissioner to prepare an interim report to the fullest extent possible and at the earliest practicable date, so that parliament may be duly informed. But there are 400 other claims outstanding, and I do not know what the decision of the Minister of Finance or of the governor in council will be with regard to those. I should think the proper way would be to make an appropriation, out of which we may pay during this fiscal year any of these 400 claims upon which awards are made by the commissioner, which are approved by order of the governor in council, and for the payment of which the government takes full responsibility when once the parliamentary appropriation is made. If my hon. friend thinks that is not the proper course, that we should allow the claims, from one end of the country to the other, some 400 or 500 in number, to wait until the ensuing session to have the awards brought before parliament and dealt with individually, well that is a program of another colour which did not occur to me as being a suitable one.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
If my hon. friend brings
in an appropriation this year and gets the consent of parliament to have money voted to meet incoming claims, at least he will have the authority of parliament. I may disagree with him on that point, and I shall discuss the matter further. But if a majority of the committee votes the estimate, at least there is nothing with which to reproach him. That, however, is not what my hon. friend has done with respect to the claims to which I have alluded. He has paid them before parliament has passed upon them.

Supply-Secretary of State

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
I was in ignorance of the previous working of the office. I went there and followed my hon. friend. I have endeavoured, so far as I could, to administer that office without fear or favour, and in each case I have rendered my very best judgment. I was advised by the departmental officers and by others, down to the auditor general, that that was an appropriation with which to pay reparations-that it had no condition tied to it but was available for the purpose for which it was used. I acted on that advice, knowing nothing of the views which my hon. friend holds. I followed that course, and if I did what was reprehensible I stand condemned.	,
Air. MACKENZIE	(Vancouver):	The
minister has informed the committee that Commissioner McDougall intends, if possible, to file a further interim report dealing only with civil claims. I speak from personal knowledge when I say that the commissioner has already heard many claims throughout Canada with respect to maltreatment of soldiers when prisoners of war, and J[ urge upon the minister, if at all possible, to have the commissioner make an interim report in regard to such of these cases as he has already decided-not civilian cases, because they will be dealt with in any case. I suggest that it would be well to have an interim report in regard to prisoners of war who suffered maltreatment. I can assure the minister that I know of hundreds of cases in the west, cases of real hardship, which I believe will be allowed by the commissioner, either in small or large degree. It would be a merciful service rendered these men if the decisions could be brought down at the earliest possible moment and the moneys paid.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
We have been taking these cases in order of precedence. A number of civil cases were left over and the hearings were completed. The awards are now being prepared. In regard to the prisoners of war, none of the oases have yet been decided, and I will tell my hon. friend why. I have had nothing to do with the hearing of these cases but I have taken a great interest in them. In many instances I have read the evidence. There is no doubt in my mind that many of our soldiers who were prisoners of war suffered very much, but owing to the lapse of years their impressions now as to the extent of their sufferings while prisoners of war are in some cases,-I do not know just the word 22110-188i
-almost fantastic. I have insisted that in respect to each claim made by prisoners of war, in addition to hearing their evidence, the records should be searched and their present statements, so far as possible, should be checked with the statements which were made, of which there is an official record, when they came back from Germany as prisoners of war; checked with the medicaTexamination which then took place, and checked also with their evidence at the later examinations which were made when they applied for pensions, because many of these men have so applied. There was not only the hearing b*y the commissioner in charge, but we also had expert medical and surgical advice which was supplied by the Department of Pensions. This work of research into the military records has taken a great deal of time, but I felt that in justice to this country and in justice fo the claimants themselves, those records should be carefully searched before an official award was made. The difficulty and delay in making that search with respect to some hundreds of men is the only reason why the awards have not been finally prepared in the large number of these military cases.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: I think it is a most extraordinary statement we have just heard from the hon. Secretary of State. He tells the committee that if a soldier who has a claim in respect of ill treatment received in Germany makes a statement, he finds that that soldier is liable to make such a fantastic statement-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: I did not say that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: -that he has to have the statement checked-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
I said that some of the
statements made now as compared with the reports which were made when they came out of Germany appeared to me in some cases to be-I searched for the word-perhaps fantastic. Perhaps "exaggerated" would be the better word. In order to check such statements I know of no other way than to check them with the military records and find out the real facts as contained therein.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
I will take the statement of my hon. friend, although I am not quite sure that that is what he said. The procedure which he is following is this: He requires far more corroboration for the story told by a soldier who has suffered ill treatment in Germany than he does for any other class of person who has claimed under these reparations.
Supply-Secretary oj State

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: Not at all.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
We have had men coming
before the commissioner to make claims because they fell into the water when some boat was torpedoed and wrecked; they got their feet wet, but here are men who spent two to three years in prisons in Germany and because they make a claim to the government for ill treatment the Secretary of State orders that that claim be checked up with the documents which he received, presumably from Germany, with documents in the possession of the pension board, with documents and statements given-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: I wish we had the German records, but we have not. We have only the statements made by these prisoners to the military officials when they returned.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: My hon. friend has not had to do with pension legislation at .all.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: I am not dealing with pension legislation.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
If he had he would know
that the soldier was so glad to get out of the army that he was willing to give any statement at the time of his discharge. I have not the slightest doubt that such was the case with the prisoners of war, and I object most strenuously, and I think many other hon. members of this house will object also, to meting out to these men different treatment from that given to others who have claimed under these reparations.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext: There is no different treatment at all.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PACIFIC FISHERMEN PISHING CONDITIONS ON BRITISH COLUMBIA COAST -STATEMENT BY MB. HANSON (SKEENA)
speechtext:
Far more corroboration is
being asked for their stories than was asked for the stories of men who claimed because they happened to be on vessels which were wrecked. They got their feet wet or lost a trunkful of luggage and the evidence shows that the most ridiculous claims were made and allowed without any corroboration being necessary. I think the Secretary of State should give at least equal treatment to those who suffered while bearing arms for their country.
